Read every sentence of 1-fast.md (edited: W307 markers now links, minutes.full 25, resilient and stem bold), calendar.md, mistakes.md, the generated sources.md, data/plan.json (plans a, b, c; gates g1 to g4; every day's task minutes re-added) and data/00-start-here/tasks.json (items []). No questions, cards, spoken items, tasks or diagrams exist for this chapter by design. calendar-preview.md is already gone from disk. Survived with verbatim support: 65 questions; 130 minutes; SAA-C03 not among the three exams in the September 2026 update (MLA-C02, SAP-C03, DVA-C03; no SAA-C04 anywhere in the corpus); domain weights 30/26/24/20; 3-month GA rule; ESL +30 once, before registering, all future registrations, and the five-step path; Pearson VUE test center or online; free 20-question sets; $29 USD per month; unanswered scored as incorrect, no guessing penalty; unscored not identified; five business days; no pass/fail on screen; 14 calendar days; full fee each attempt; 150 USD; compensatory model; 720 scaled; 24-hour and twice-only reschedule; best available answer; questions replaced after a change. Findings are about sentences that say more than their links or contradict the chapter's own numbers, plan logic, and omissions that change what the reader pays or when she gets a result.

findings.section: plan-a (paragraph after the Plan A table)
findings.quote: A mock is one full Tutorials Dojo practice exam in timed mode, in one quiet two-hour block. Then review it for about 1 hour, with the cause codes of `mistakes.md`. Pace: 2 minutes or less per question, then your flagged questions.
findings.evidence: Fact exam-duration-minutes: 'Exam duration: "130 minutes"' (www/certification/certified-solutions-architect-associate, line 'Exam duration' / '130 minutes'), and the same file says 'So train at 130 minutes and sit at 160.' A two-hour block is 120 minutes, 10 minutes shorter than the time the reader is told to train at, so a full timed mock does not fit the block. The pace is also wrong: fact exam-question-count '65 questions; either multiple choice or multiple response'; 65 x 2 minutes = 130 minutes, the whole exam, which leaves no time for 'then your flagged questions' at 130 minutes. Fix: 'in one quiet block of 130 minutes' (2 hours 10 minutes), and a pace that leaves time for flags, e.g. 'about 1 minute 45 seconds per question, which leaves about 15 minutes for flagged questions'. The 180-minute mock rows still fit (130 + about 50 minutes of review), so say 'review it for about 50 minutes' or keep 180 and say so.
findings.resolution: calendar.md plan-a: mock block is now 130 minutes (linked to exam-duration-minutes), review about 50 minutes (fits the 180-minute mock days), pace about 1 minute 45 seconds per question, leaving about 15 minutes for questions marked with Flag for Review (exam-timer-and-review).

findings.quote: So the softer rule allows one domain at 65%. <!-- no-fact: plan -->
findings.evidence: The gate row it explains says 'Both 75% or more, no domain under 65%, 10 minutes left' (data/plan.json g2: 'no domain under 65%'). 'No domain under 65%' allows every domain to be at 65% or more, not one domain. The reader skims and reads 'one' as a cap: with two domains at 66% she would move the exam although her own rule says go. The cited fact supports weak domains in general, not a count: exam-compensatory-scoring 'you do not need to achieve a passing score in each section. You need to pass only the overall exam.' Fix: 'So the softer rule lets a domain be as low as 65%.'
findings.resolution: calendar.md readiness-gates: 'So a weak domain alone does not fail you, but the softer rule keeps a floor of 65% for each domain.' (no-fact: plan).

findings.section: plan-a (Plan A table, Day 9) and plan-c (Plan C table, Day 10); data/plan.json a.d09, c.d10
findings.quote: | Day 9 | 60 | 18 AWS Lambda (Fast); 40 High availability and disaster recovery (Pass); 41 Cost optimization (Fast) |
findings.evidence: Rule broken: the chapter's own route table (1-fast.md, three-routes) gives a deep chapter 'About 20 minutes' on Fast and 'About 50 minutes' on Pass. Registry (data/book.json): 18, 40 and 41 are all tier deep. data/plan.json a.d09 budgets 40 (Pass) at 25 minutes and 41 (Fast) at 15, so Day 9 is about 20 + 50 + 20 = 90 minutes, not 60. Every other deep Pass task in plan.json is 45 to 65 minutes; 25 is the medium Pass value. The same 30 minutes are missing from Plan C Day 10 (220 should be about 250). Plan A becomes about 41.75 hours and Plan C about 29.7: the 'about' totals survive, the day rows do not. Fix: d09 = 90 (40 Pass 50, 41 Fast 20) and c.d10 = 250, or change 40 to Fast and say why (diagnostic Resilient 71%).
findings.resolution: data/plan.json a.d09: 40 Pass 50, 41 Fast 20, day 90; c.d10: same, day 250. Totals re-added: A 2,505 min (about 42 h; 39 without mock 5), B 2,855 (about 48 h), C 1,780 (about 30 h); calendar.md and the preview note updated.

findings.section: plan-c (paragraph after the Plan C table); data/plan.json gate g3
findings.quote: Its gate is weaker: 70% or more on mock 1 and 75% or more on mock 2. <!-- no-fact: plan --> If a mock misses its mark, move the exam to Day 19 and continue with Plan A Day 13 the next day.
findings.evidence: (1) Day labels do not line up. The Plan C gate is on Day 11 (g3, day d11). Plan A Day 13 on Day 12 puts Plan A Day 14 (mock 3, Gate 1) on Day 13, Plan A Day 18 (review sheets, stop by 18:00) on Day 17 and Plan A Day 19 (exam-day warm-up) on Day 18, while the exam is on Day 19: one day is left without a plan and every later Plan A label is one day off. (2) 'If a mock misses its mark' lets the reader act after mock 1 on Day 9; 'the next day' is then Day 10, and Plan A Day 13 replaces Plan C Day 10, so 40 High availability, 11 and 12 networking and 18 Lambda are never studied. g3 says the check is 'after mock 2'. Fix: 'Decide after mock 2 on Day 11. If mock 1 was under 70% or mock 2 is under 75%, move the exam to Day 19. Do Plan A Day 13 on Day 12, then follow Plan A from Day 14 one day early, with a light day on Day 18.'
findings.resolution: calendar.md plan-c and plan.json g3: decide after mock 2 on Day 11; on a miss move the exam to Day 19, do Plan A Days 13 to 17 on Days 12 to 16 (skip what is done), then a light day and Plan A Days 18 and 19.

findings.section: do-this-today (steps 2 and 3); calendar.md readiness-gates (last trap and closing line); data/plan.json g4
findings.quote: 2. **Then book Day 19 of Plan A.** ... 3. **Take the free official practice set.** ... Take the SAA-C03 set first, as your baseline.
findings.evidence: The plan choice depends on the practice set (calendar.md plan-c: 'Choose it only if your Day 1 practice set is 70% or more'; g4 'Plan choice' on d01), but step 2 books Plan A Day 19 before step 3 produces that score. A reader who then qualifies for Plan C must reschedule once to Day 13; if the Plan C gate fails she reschedules again to Day 19. Fact exam-reschedule-limit: 'Each exam appointment can only be rescheduled twice. If you need to reschedule your exam a third time, you will need to cancel your exam and schedule it for a more convenient date.' (before-testing). The chapter itself says 'Each plan switch uses one of the two.' So on the Plan C path both reschedules are gone before Gate 1 or Gate 2 can send her to Plan B. Fix: swap steps 2 and 3 ('Take the practice set, then book Day 19 of Plan A, or Day 13 if you choose Plan C'), keeping ESL +30 first.
findings.resolution: 1-fast.md do-this-today reordered: 1 ESL +30, 2 practice set, 3 choose a plan in calendar.md, check the deadline, then book. plan.json d01 of all plans gains 'Choose your plan, then book the exam' after the practice set; g4 says book after choosing.

findings.quote: Count five business days from Day 23: if that passes your deadline, Plan B does not fit.
findings.evidence: Fact exam-results-timing: 'Final results will be posted to your AWS Certification Account within five business days after the close of the exam.' (after-testing), and exam-no-result-on-screen: 'Most AWS Certification exams do not display your pass/fail result at the end of the test.' (faqs). This holds for every exam date, not only Plan B. READER.md: 'Pass SAA-C03 by Oct 31, 2026 (date not booked)'. With Day 1 on Oct 13, Plan A Day 19 is Oct 31, so even Plan A's result can arrive after the deadline; the plan the reader is told to book ('Start with Plan A', 'Then book Day 19 of Plan A') is the one that is never checked. Fix: move the check to how-to-use-this-calendar: 'Before you book, count five business days from your exam day. If that passes your deadline, move Day 1 earlier or choose a shorter plan.'
findings.resolution: calendar.md how-to-use-this-calendar: 'Before you book, add five business days to your exam day: final results arrive within five business days. If that passes your deadline, read Plan C.' Step 3 of 1-fast.md says check your deadline in calendar.md.

findings.quote: So after an exam on Day 13, the earliest retake is Day 27. To keep one retake before a deadline, take the first exam [14 calendar days](../facts/exam.md#exam-retake-wait) or more before it.
findings.evidence: The rule counts only the wait. A retake on the deadline day gives its result up to five business days later: exam-results-timing 'Final results will be posted to your AWS Certification Account within five business days after the close of the exam.' And the first result is not on screen (exam-no-result-on-screen), so the reader learns that she failed only when results arrive, which is when she can book the retake. The same file applies the five-business-day check to Plan B but not here. Fix: 'To keep one retake with its result before a deadline, take the first exam 14 calendar days plus about one week (five business days) or more before it.'
findings.resolution: calendar.md plan-c: the result of the retake arrives within five business days (exam-results-timing); 'To fit a retake and its result before a deadline, book the first exam 14 calendar days plus five business days ahead, or earlier.'

findings.quote: You also pay the [full registration fee for each exam attempt](../facts/exam.md#exam-retake-attempts-and-fee), [150 USD](../facts/exam.md#exam-cost) for this exam.
findings.evidence: READER.md: 'Passed AWS Cloud Practitioner.' Verified fact exam-discount-next-exam, under the question 'Are there any savings on exams if I already hold an active AWS Certification?': 'Yes. Once you earn one AWS Certification, you get 50% discount on your next AWS Certification exam. You can sign in and access this discount in your AWS Certification Account.' (www/certification/certified-solutions-architect-associate). before-testing also: 'Vouchers that are intended to cover 50% of an exam will be valid for 50% off of the exam price at the time of exam purchase'. The trap sentence is true as a list price, but the chapter never tells the reader that the booking in step 2 can use her 50% discount, so she will likely pay 150 USD instead of 75 USD. Fix: in step 2 add 'If your Cloud Practitioner certification is active, use the [50% discount](../facts/exam.md#exam-discount-next-exam) in your AWS Certification Account.' Keep the trap for the retake.
findings.resolution: 1-fast.md step 3: 'look for a [50% discount on your next AWS Certification exam](exam-discount-next-exam)'. The trap keeps the full fee for a retake.

findings.quote: When a service changes, AWS will [replace exam questions determined to be impacted by the change](../facts/exam.md#exam-changed-service-questions-replaced). So a D miss usually comes from older practice material.
findings.evidence: The link does not support 'usually', and the page around it points the other way. www/certification/faqs follows the replacement answer with a separate question, 'How should I answer a question that I think has been affected by a change in a service or feature?', answered 'Choose the best available answer from the options in the question.' (fact exam-choose-best-available-answer, already linked in the D line). AWS thus expects affected questions to reach real candidates; the replacement has no stated time. No source gives a frequency for dated practice material. Fix: drop 'So' and 'usually': 'Older practice material often assumes old limits. AWS replaces affected exam questions over time; if a question on the exam still looks dated, choose the best available answer.'
findings.resolution: mistakes.md: 'So ... usually' removed; now 'Older practice material can assume old limits. When a service changes, AWS will replace exam questions ... If a question on the exam still looks dated, choose the best available answer.'

findings.quote: most exams show [no pass or fail on screen](../facts/exam.md#exam-no-result-on-screen)
findings.evidence: RULINGS, 'Displays of number-free facts (2026-10-11)': 'A display of a fact without numbers is a short phrase (at most 8 words) copied verbatim from one of the fact's quotes, never a paraphrase: the re-derivation audit matches displays word for word.' The only quote of exam-no-result-on-screen is 'Most AWS Certification exams do not display your pass/fail result at the end of the test.' The phrase 'no pass or fail on screen' is not in it, so this link fails the W14 audit although lint accepts it (it is a registered display of chapter 01). Fix here: 'most exams [do not display your pass/fail result](../facts/exam.md#exam-no-result-on-screen) at the end of the test'; and file a fact request for chapter 01 to drop the paraphrased display.
findings.resolution: calendar.md plan-b: link text is now the verbatim display 'do not display your pass/fail result at the end of the test'. The paraphrased display 'no pass or fail on screen' of exam-no-result-on-screen is no longer used in chapter 00; dropping it from the fact is a chapter-01 registrar decision, no request filed from this chapter.

findings.quote: Scores are [scaled scores, rather than the raw number of questions scored correct](../facts/exam.md#exam-scaled-scoring). So no mock percentage converts to it.
findings.evidence: (1) The display is 11 words, over the 8-word limit for number-free displays (RULINGS, Displays of number-free facts); mistakes.md '[replace exam questions determined to be impacted by the change]' is 10 words. Shorter verbatim phrases exist: 'reported as scaled scores' (after-testing quote) and 'replace exam questions' (faqs quote). (2) 'no mock percentage converts to it' is true of Tutorials Dojo percentages, but AWS's own Official Practice Exam reports on the exam's scale: certification-prep 'take a full-length Official Practice Exam. You can choose to review the answers, or choose not to, and get a scaled score.' (fact exam-official-practice-exam-scaled-score). Fix: 'So no percentage from a third-party mock converts to it.'
findings.resolution: (2) fixed: 'So no third-party mock percentage converts to it.' (1) rejected for chapter 00: both displays are registered and copied verbatim from the fact quotes, so the word-for-word audit matches them; the 8-word display cap is the chapter-01 registrar's merge check.

findings.quote: Go: the softer rule. A later date leaves no retake either.
findings.evidence: The sentence came from the preview, where it rested on fixed dates (an exam near Oct 23 against an October deadline). The chapter removed all dates ('No dates, because your Day 1 is not fixed'), so the sentence now states as a general fact something that depends on the reader's Day 1 and deadline. With Day 1 three or more weeks before the deadline it is false (fact exam-retake-wait: 14 calendar days). Fix: 'If your deadline leaves no time for a retake after Day 23, a later date gives you no retake either.' or drop the sentence.
findings.resolution: calendar.md Gate 2 softer row: the date-dependent sentence 'A later date leaves no retake either.' is removed.

findings.section: readiness-gates (last Exam trap and closing sentence)
findings.quote: Each appointment can [only be rescheduled twice](../facts/exam.md#exam-reschedule-limit). ... Each plan switch uses one of the two.
findings.evidence: The AWS sentence continues: 'If you need to reschedule your exam a third time, you will need to cancel your exam and schedule it for a more convenient date.' (before-testing, quoted in exam-reschedule-limit), and 'Individuals who cancel their exam more than 24 hours before their scheduled appointment will be refunded the exam fee they paid at the time of purchase.' (exam-reschedule-window). A third switch is possible by cancel and re-book; the trap reads as a hard cap. Fix: add 'A third change means cancel and book again.' (display 'a third time' exists on exam-reschedule-limit).
findings.resolution: calendar.md reschedule trap: 'To change it [a third time](exam-reschedule-limit), you cancel the exam and schedule it again.' Plan B also says a later move can be the third.

findings.quote: [ESL +30](../facts/exam.md#exam-esl-accommodation) is a [30-minute exam extension](../facts/exam.md#exam-esl-accommodation) for non-native English speakers.
findings.evidence: before-testing, English as a second language: 'A 30-minute exam extension is available upon request to non-native English speakers when taking an exam in English.' The condition 'when taking an exam in English' is dropped here and in 'So train at 130 minutes and sit at 160.' The reader takes the exam in English, so her plan is right, but the rule is stated without its scope. The same page, three lines above, says 'Accommodations must be requested prior to scheduling each exam.' (fact exam-accommodation-before-scheduling), which a reader who opens the page sees next to 'only needs to be requested once'. Fix: add 'when you take the exam in English', and optionally one clause: 'The each-exam rule on that page is for other accommodations.'
findings.resolution: 1-fast.md step 1: 'for non-native English speakers who take the exam in English'; ESL spelled out in both files. The optional clause about the each-exam rule is not added: it would be an interpretation of the page layout without a quote.

findings.quote: The paid [Official Practice Exams](../facts/exam.md#exam-skill-builder-individual-subscription) are optional: a Skill Builder subscription [starts at $29 USD per month](../facts/exam.md#exam-skill-builder-individual-subscription).
findings.evidence: 'Optional' is true (not required), but AWS frames it the other way: certification-prep 'Once you feel prepared, take a full-length Official Practice Exam. You can choose to review the answers, or choose not to, and get a scaled score. This is a highly recommended step prior to attempting the exam.' (fact exam-official-practice-exam-scaled-score), and the SAA page's step 4 'Assess your exam readiness: Take the AWS Certification Official Practice Exam.' It is also the only practice that reports on the 720 scale, which the 720 trap says no mock percentage converts to. Fix: 'The paid Official Practice Exam is the only practice with a scaled score; AWS calls it a [highly recommended step](...). One month of Skill Builder [starts at $29 USD per month](...).' (needs a short verbatim display on exam-official-practice-exam-scaled-score).
findings.resolution: The paid Official Practice Exam moved to the calendar's optional list: 'where you [get a scaled score](exam-official-practice-exam-scaled-score); Skill Builder [starts at $29 USD per month]'. The word 'optional' framing is gone from 1-fast.md (word budget L201).

findings.quote: Choose it only if your Day 1 practice set is 70% or more and a recorded fail costs you nothing. <!-- no-fact: plan -->
findings.evidence: The threshold is the book's own and is marked, but it rests on a tool AWS presents for format, not readiness: certification-prep 'Use the free Practice Question Sets to understand the exam format better. Once you feel prepared, take a full-length Official Practice Exam.' The set has 20 questions (exam-official-practice-question-sets 'These 20-question sets'), so 70% is 14 right answers and one question moves the result by 5 points. Fix: one clause that 20 questions is a rough signal, or add a second condition from a longer test (READER: diagnostic 69% on 65 questions).
findings.resolution: calendar.md plan-c: 'The free [20-question sets] give a rough signal, so also accept the cost of a fail (see the trap below).'

findings.section: three-routes (route table and the paragraphs after it)
findings.quote: | Pass | Fast, the core questions, the subsections your misses point to, one spoken answer | About 50 minutes; 65 minutes for 03, 10, 16 and 21 | About 22 minutes | ... These subsections carry a mark for the Pass route.
findings.evidence: (1) The first finished deep chapter already differs: 03-iam/1-fast.md front matter 'minutes: {fast: 20, pass: 73, full: 174}', against the table's 65 minutes (Pass, 03) and about 2 hours 15 minutes (Full, deep); calendar Day 1 budgets 03 IAM (Pass) at 65 (data/plan.json a.d01.t5). The chapter does say 'When the chapter and this table differ, use the chapter', so Day 1 is about 173 minutes, not 165. (2) The Pass mark is only the HTML comment '<!-- section: route=pass -->' (03-iam/2-deep.md lines 87, 165, 245; exemplar iam-2-deep.md line 23), which a Markdown reader does not see. Fix: re-derive the Pass and Full times after more deep chapters exist or say 'at least'; say 'In the web version, these subsections carry a Pass mark', or add a visible marker.
findings.resolution: (1) Full deep time is now 'About 2 to 3 hours'; the Pass row keeps its estimate and the existing line 'When the chapter and this table differ, use the chapter' governs (IAM 73). (2) The sentence about an invisible Pass mark is removed.

findings.quote: Speak for 10 minutes every day, standing.
findings.evidence: Plan A's 'about 41 hours' (sum of data/plan.json a day minutes = 2,475) counts speaking only on Days 3, 4 and 8 ('1 spoken answer', 10 minutes; the 45-minute rehearsal). Ten minutes on the other 16 days adds about 2.7 hours that no total shows, against the reader's budget of about 40 study hours (READER.md). Fix: 'Speaking is not in the day totals: add about 3 hours' in plan-a, or add 10 minutes to each day.
findings.resolution: calendar.md optional list: 'Speaking for 10 minutes each day: about 3 hours in all.'

findings.quote: The calendar names the route of each chapter.
findings.evidence: calendar.md and data/plan.json give no route for 44 Reference architectures, 45 Decision atlas, 46, 47, 48 and 52 (route null), and the light chapters 20, 30, 36 and 49 are only listed as optional. calendar.md plan-a also says 'A row names each chapter by its number, the start of its title and its route.' Fix: 'The calendar names the route of each service chapter.' in both places.
findings.resolution: 1-fast.md: 'The calendar gives each service chapter a route.' calendar.md plan-a: 'and, for a service chapter, its route.'
